do_not_assume: A valid item means the page block selects it.
goal: An item is structurally complete, correctly scheduled, reviewable, and eligible for display.
steps: Identify the destination channel and inspect its channel type, item attributes, date mode, approval requirement, and personalization setting.
Enter the item through `Tools > Content` unless channel administration is required.
Populate the required fields and structured item attributes.
Set Start and optional Expire dates according to the channel type.
Add or create child items only after confirming the allowed child channels.
If the channel requires approval, leave or move the item into the appropriate review state and have a user with Approval permission complete approval.
Inspect the exact rendering block’s channel, status, filters, ordering, and template.
Verify the public result in both pre-start or expired and active conditions as applicable. (Add Content Items, Manage Content Items)
Confirm that the expected page uses the intended Content Channel View or Content Channel Item View block and the intended channel.
Check the item’s approval status and whether the channel requires approval.
Check Start and Expire dates using the date model defined by the channel type.
Inspect block status filters, item filters, context filters, route parameters, and ordering.
If the item contains Lava, verify that the item-view block processes `Item.Content` with `RunLava`.
If personalization is enabled, inspect the channel setting, item assignments, and the block’s Ignore, Prioritize, or Filter choice.
Check View and Interact permissions separately.
If the content is being rendered through RSS, test without current-person or page-context assumptions. (Add a Content Channel Item, Content Channel View Block, Personalize Content Channel Items)
title: Recipe: Publish a governed Content Channel Item

do_not_assume: Segment membership updates in real time.
A channel setting controls how the block applies matches.
One browser session is enough to prove audience isolation.
goal: Matching visitors receive the intended filtered or prioritized content without cross-visitor cache leakage.
steps: Enable personalization on the exact site.
Enable Visitor Tracking if activity-based or anonymous continuity is required.
Create or validate the Personalization Segments and Request Filters.
For Person Filters, confirm the backing data views are persisted.
Enable personalization on the Content Channel.
Assign segments and/or Request Filters to each target item.
Remember that multiple segments are OR within their group, multiple Request Filters are OR within their group, and using both groups requires one match from each.
Configure the Content Channel View block as Ignore, Prioritize, or Filter.
Disable output caching.
Run Update Personalization Data when segment membership has changed.
Test a matching identified person, a nonmatching person, and an anonymous or request-filter context. (Personalize Content Channel Items, Troubleshoot Personalization)
title: Recipe: Add personalization to Content Channel Items

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: A persisted segment and its browser-facing membership state reflect current person data.
steps: Identify the segment and each persisted data view used by its Person Filter.
Refresh the underlying persisted data view.
Run Update Personalization Data.
Inspect the segment’s current person list.
Account for the `ROCK_SEGMENT_FILTERS` cookie affinity duration.
Retest with the intended person and site.
If the result remains wrong, evaluate every filter area and its Any or All logic. (Update Personalization Job, Troubleshoot Personalization)
title: Recipe: Refresh personalization membership

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: Multiple channels or calendars are searchable together with deliberate filtering, ranking, and security boundaries.
steps: Confirm an active Universal Search index component.
Create or select the collection under `Admin Tools > CMS Configuration > Content Collections`.
Add the required content channels and calendars.
Select the source attributes that should be indexed.
Enable and arrange the collection’s search filters.
Configure trending only if interaction logging exists on the item-viewing surfaces.
Configure segment and Request Filter evaluation if personalized ranking is required.
Rebuild the index.
Configure a Content Collection View block with the collection, result count, search behavior, filters, templates, sort orders, and personalization boost.
Verify that each visible filter is enabled in both the collection and block.
Audit every source for restricted content before public display. (Set Up Content Collections, Content Collection View)
Confirm the expected channel or calendar is a source in the collection.
Confirm the needed item attributes were selected for indexing.
Run `Index Content Collections` or use Rebuild Index after same-day changes.
Confirm filters are enabled both in the collection and in the Content Collection View block.
Recheck the block’s selected collection, search-on-load behavior, result count, and templates.
If personalization is involved, verify site personalization and the block’s boost configuration.
Stop before exposing the collection if it contains restricted items; individual item security is not enforced by the collection. (Troubleshoot Content Collections, Content Collection View)
title: Recipe: Build and refresh a Content Collection

do_not_assume: Avoid output caching if any rendered value varies by visitor.
goal: Editors can change structured content without editing presentation markup.
steps: In Rock 19.0, open `Admin Tools > CMS Configuration > Content Component Templates`.
Copy a suitable existing template as a starting point when appropriate.
Build Display Lava using related content items and component settings.
Temporarily use `{{ 'Lava' | Debug }}` to inspect available context.
Remove debug output.
Create Content Channel Item attribute categories whose names exactly match each target template.
Add item attributes to the applicable categories; leave Categories blank only when the attribute should appear for every template.
Configure the block’s template, filters, item multiplicity, and presentation values.
Avoid output caching if any rendered value varies by visitor.
Test editing and rendering without requiring the editor to modify HTML. (Create Content Component Templates, Add Content Component Item Attributes)
title: Recipe: Configure a Content Component template

do_not_assume: A changed attribute default updates existing item values.
Text that resembles a Boolean or date is valid for every target field type.
goal: A scheduled job safely writes evaluated Lava output into a compatible target attribute.
steps: Add a Lava-type item attribute to hold the expression.
Add the target item attribute with the required field type.
Populate and test the Lava on representative items.
Confirm its output is valid for the target field type.
Create a Content Channel Item Self Update job for the channel.
Set Template Key to the Lava attribute key.
Set Target Key to the target attribute key.
Run the job in a controlled test and inspect the affected item values.
Configure page Lava to use the target attribute.
Create a separate job for each additional channel. (Self Update Content Channel Items)
Confirm that the user has View permission on the channel; that controls whether the channel appears under `Tools > Content`.
Clear or adjust the status, date-range, and title filters.
If the item is pending, use the pending-only channel toggle to locate the channel.
Confirm that approvals are enabled for the channel.
Confirm that the user’s role has `Approve` on `Rock.Model.ContentChannelType`.
For missing add/delete controls, record the installed version and determine whether the Rock 19.3 fix applies. (Manage Content Items, Secure Content, Rock Core Release Notes)
title: Recipe: Automate a channel item attribute with Lava

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: A media item appears through normal content tools with the intended player behavior and analytics.
steps: Confirm the Media Account and provider plugin, or identify that the Local Media Account is being maintained manually.
Add a Media Element item attribute to the target Content Channel.
Either link the Media Element manually or enable channel synchronization on the Media Folder.
Confirm that a newly added element creates the expected item when synchronization is used.
In the display Lava, read the Media Element attribute’s raw value.
Pass the GUID to the Media Player shortcode’s `media` parameter.
Configure auto-resume and play-combination windows deliberately.
Play the media from the published page and inspect the resulting analytics.
If a direct variant is needed instead, select its URL from Media Files and use `src`, recognizing that this is a different integration pattern. (Publishing Media, Use With Content Channel Items)
title: Recipe: Publish a Media Element through a channel

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: An item is uploaded or downloaded with its license and overwrite behavior understood.
steps: Enable Content Library features on the source or destination channel as appropriate.
For upload, confirm the channel license and populate the item’s Experience Level and Topic.
Upload only the selected item.
For download, start from the destination channel’s **Download from Library** action.
Select and download the library item.
Before downloading it again, identify any local edits.
Refresh only when overwriting those local edits is acceptable.
Preserve the license and required attribution in downstream presentation. (Set Up The Content Library, Library Viewer)
Confirm **Enable Personalization** on the exact site.
If browsing activity is required, confirm Enable Visitor Tracking on that site.
Confirm the item’s channel has personalization enabled.
Evaluate every segment filter area and its internal Any or All logic.
Refresh the persisted data view when person data has changed.
Run Update Personalization Data.
Allow for or inspect the `ROCK_SEGMENT_FILTERS` cookie affinity interval.
Evaluate Request Filters against the current site, device, query, cookie, IP, location, day, and time.
Confirm the rendering block is not set to Ignore.
Disable output caching for personalized output and retest in isolated sessions. (Configure Site for Personalization, Troubleshoot Personalization, Configure Content Components)
title: Recipe: Share or refresh Content Library material

do_not_assume: Stop if gateway currency and organization currency do not agree.
goal: Numeric values display the intended currency symbol without implying conversion or silently changing gateway behavior.
steps: Confirm the organization’s intended transaction currency.
Confirm every relevant payment gateway uses the matching currency.
Set Organization Currency Code for the intended display symbol.
Use `FormatAsCurrency` for numeric currency output in Lava.
Test display values and payment processing as separate checks.
Stop if gateway currency and organization currency do not agree. (Localize Currency)
Identify whether the problem concerns display, entry validation, or downstream processing.
For dates and times, inspect server culture in System Information.
For phones, inspect Phone Country Code ordering, regular expressions, and formatting expressions.
For currency display, inspect Organization Currency Code and Lava formatting.
Independently confirm payment-gateway currency; a symbol change does not reconfigure it.

For addresses, confirm Support International Addresses and the selected country’s labels, format, and states. (Localize Dates & Times, Localize Phone Numbers, Localize Currency, Configure International Addresses)
title: Recipe: Configure localized currency display safely
